messages:
maya: Hey team — running into a weird parity bug between the Node and Python sample apps when using the embeddings + rerank helper. Node SDK returns 1536-d vectors consistently, Python sometimes returns 1536 and sometimes 768 for identical inputs. Also seeing duplicate items submitted when auth refresh happens mid-batch. Anyone seen this? :confused:

maya: Repro summary: small batch (3 items) using the batching helper -> sometimes the client gets a 401, the helper retries and whole batch gets re-sent so we end up with duplicates in the upstream rerank request. Vector dims also mismatch intermittently. Minimal JS snippet below (using official sample app helper):

maya: ```js
const {batcher, embeddings} = require('redwood-sdksample');
const items = [{id: 'a', text:'...'}, {id:'b', text:'...'}, {id:'c', text:'...'}];
await batcher.send(items, async (batch) => {
  return await embeddings.create({model: 'open-embed-1536', inputs: batch.map(x => x.text)});
});
```

tom: ugh. can you paste the exact SDK versions and the raw response for both languages? Also do you use client-side dedupe? :eyes:

maya: Node: 0.22.0, sample-app branch main. Python sample app: 0.21.4 pinned. Raw-ish responses: Node response shows `data[0].embedding.length = 1536`. Python sometimes shows `embedding.length = 768`. Headers show `x-request-id` present. Logs show:```
maya:  2026-03-22T14:03:21Z ERROR embedding request 401 token_expired
maya:  2026-03-22T14:03:22Z INFO retrying batch id=8314 attempt=2
maya:  2026-03-22T14:03:22Z INFO sending batch id=8314 items=3
maya:  2026-03-22T14:03:22Z WARN upstream rerank received duplicate ids: ["a","b"]
```

liam: That log pattern suggests the batching helper's retry semantics requeue the whole batch rather than replaying only the failed request. We fixed something similar for streaming calls last quarter. Can you confirm if Python helper is using `normalize_embeddings=True` by default? There was a change that resizes vectors when model aliasing occurs.

maya: Checking — Python sample app config: `EMBED_NORMALIZE` env unset (should default false). But I can repro with both envs. Also noticed Python SDK includes the key `embedding_vector` in the response body for some runs instead of `embedding`. Example: { "embedding_vector": [...768 numbers...] } whereas Node is { "embedding": [...1536 numbers...] }. So two orthogonal issues: key/name inconsistency and dim mismatch.

olga: Temporary workaround: dedupe on server side by `id` before rerank + assert dims equal before scoring. Ugly but works. Filed internal issue for unify-shape. Also, if you can, set client-side unique batch ids so we can map duplicates to original batch.

ben: From SDK team — thanks for the clear repro, @maya. We're tracking two defects: (1) retry behavior in the batcher re-sends entire batch on auth-refresh -> duplicate submits, and (2) an inconsistent response shape between language SDKs where older Python branch still returns `embedding_vector` for a transitional model name. I've created a test and a patch for the retry logic that will only requeue the failing request(s) on 401 rather than full batch. Will also normalize the response key to `embedding` across SDKs.

ben: Quick ask: can you attach the request/response IDs for one of the failing runs? `x-request-id` and the batch id printed in logs would be ideal. I'll link to the automated test.

maya: Pasted two request ids in DM. Also note that the rerank endpoint expects `vectors` in index order; the helper might be shuffling when it dedupes. Saw a test where order changed.

sdk-bot: Issue created: GRW-4821 "batcher: avoid full-batch retries on auth refresh". Assigned to @ben, linked PR 5023. CI tests failing on python-expander shape.

ben: Patch in PR 5023 updates retry behavior and adds a cross-sdk shape compatibility layer. We'll try to cut a patch release v0.22.1 for Node and v0.21.5 for Python tomorrow.

maya: Great — thanks. Will re-test with the patch and report back. For the record: onboarding experience is rough when sample apps disagree like this (took me an hour to triage). Might be worth an onboarding note in the sample app README about SDK parity and a quick `verify-shape` script. :+1:

olga: Agreed — adding a tiny `verify_vectors.py`/`verify_vectors.js` to the onboarding checklist would save time.

tom: thank you! if you hit any other oddities ping #devex and tag @ben. :thumbsup:
